correctness.rationale: Manhattan geodesic betweenness yields the strict-incomparability and excluded-axis criterion for corner triples. Count antitone diagonals of subrectangles minus crossing-axis pairs. Any four-set through a corner would have three pairwise incomparable points, whose middle in coordinate order is geodesically between the extremes. Explicit witnesses extend every other corner pair; the only maximal pairs are both neighbors and the antipodal corner. The canonical bipartite neighbor reply proves Builder-first two, and a corner Blocker opening caps the primed game at three. Every starting vertex embeds in an isometric 2x3 grid partitioned into two explicit general-position triples, proving primed lower three outside the four-cycle. A BFS-distance exhaustive verifier checks 18 grids (20,504 exact minimax states and 72 rooted classifications). The unrestricted proof does not depend on finite enumeration.

originality.rationale: The 2023 founding paper proves the Builder-first bipartite value but does not give Blocker-first values for rectangular Cartesian grids; it explicitly requests new families of Blocker-first value three. The 2024 full grid general-position polynomial counts all feasible configurations without determining corner-rooted inclusion-maximal sets or adversarial optimal lengths. The 2025 survey distinguishes avoidance/achievement from minimax games. The 2026 mutual-visibility paper concerns a different game on nongeodetic grids. Actual research-record searches for aliases and implication-dominating results found no covering theorem, and 102 accessible own historical claims were checked for duplication. Residual unindexed priority risk remains.
residual_risks: No bibliographic search can rule out all unindexed or independently published equivalent results.

value.rationale: A complete infinite family of nontrivial path-grid Cartesian products has exact two-player game values with a sharp 2x2 exception, answering a natural instance of the published request to classify Blocker-first value-three graphs (arXiv:2310.19949, Problem 5.7). The proof additionally gives the full size-specific corner-rooted maximal configuration count, not present in the published unrooted grid polynomial. The question is canonical and strategically motivated; not an arbitrary finite slice or a trivial relabeling.
